references.text: Jacob's blessing over Gad, where it is prophesied that Gad will be attacked but will strike back. This forms the basis for Moses' blessing over Gad.
The tribe of Gad asks to settle east of the Jordan because of their large number of livestock. This shows Gad's expansion and territory as blessed by Moses.
Joshua blesses the tribe of Gad after they have fulfilled their military duty. This confirms their warrior nature mentioned in Moses' blessing.
Gad is mentioned as a tribe living near the Jordan. The verse describes their settlement pattern, which relates to the expansion of their territory.
The tribe of Gad is described as brave warriors, skilled in battle. This matches the image of the lion tearing its prey apart.
The Gadites are described as warriors with faces like lions, swift as gazelles. The lion metaphor is repeated from Moses' blessing.
Israel is compared to a lioness that rises and a lion that does not lie down until it has devoured its prey. A similar lion image is used for Gad.
